summary.short: Establishes the Data Protection Commission and gives further effect in Ireland to the GDPR and the law-enforcement data Directive, setting national rules on children's data, automated decisions, special-category processing, law-enforcement processing and enforcement. Dated 24 May 2018; commencement by ministerial order.
summary.long: Number 7 of 2018 establishes the Data Protection Commission as supervisory authority (Part 2) and gives further effect to the GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679) and to Directive (EU) 2016/680 on criminal-law processing (long title). Part 3 sets national rules within the GDPR: a child is a person under 18 (s.29); the consent age for information society services is 16 (s.31); processing a child's data for direct marketing, profiling or micro-targeting is an offence (s.30); solely automated decisions may be authorised by enactment with safeguards (s.57); and special-category processing and rights restrictions are permitted for listed purposes (ss.45-61). Part 4 deals with transfers from the 1988 Act. Part 5 sets duties for controllers and processors handling personal data for criminal-law purposes, including records, impact assessments and breach notification to the Commission (ss.69-88). Part 6 covers complaints, inquiries, corrective powers, administrative fines (s.141), offences (a maximum of EUR 50,000 on indictment under s.4(2)(b)) and judicial remedies. Parts 7 and 8 cover courts and amend other Acts. The Act comes into operation on days the Minister appoints (s.1(3)).

notes: Part 1 of 3: covers the contents list, the Acts Referred To list, the long title and sections 1 to 88 (through Part 5, Chapter 3). Sections 89 to 232, Part 8 amendments and the Schedules are not in this part. target_instrument_id, lei and ticker are empty strings because no registry IDs or identifiers were supplied. Internal point: section 29 defines child as under 18 for the Regulation, while section 31(1) sets the Article 8 age at 16. Section 30 applies the section 29 definition. Section 7(4) disapplies the repeals for section 8(1)(b), (2) and (3). Section_status entries are required by the schema; relations and entities are populated. Part 2 of 3 covers ss.89 to 214; the text ends at the heading of s.214 with no operative text. Relations to the Regulation and the Directive come from defined terms; the Directive is not named in this part and no target IDs are given (empty strings where no registry ID is available). Part 8 amends many further enactments; only those with headings in this part are listed. s.129(3) refers to section 24 of the Act of 1988, covered by the amendment row. Thresholds such as the €75,000 court-selection limit (s.142(6)) and the €1,000,000 fine cap for public bodies (s.141(4)) are not coded in this part. Part 3 of 3 covers s. 12, ss. 215 to 232, Schedules 1 to 3 and footnotes 39 to 54. Most provisions are textual amendments to other Acts, coded here as relations; they are not coded as obligations or thresholds of this Act.
